chunks: And as for what was narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ibn Muskan from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The eating of any of the wild beasts is not suitable; indeed, I dislike it and consider it repulsive."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating wild animals in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam Al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expresses a strong personal aversion to consuming wild beasts (*al-siba'*), characterizing it with *karahat tanzih* (recommended dislike) rather than strict prohibition (*haram*). This reflects the Shia juristic principle that the Prophet’s and Imams’ personal preferences often serve as a guide for recommended acts, distinguishing between what is merely disliked and what is legally forbidden. The term *qadhar* (repulsive) underscores the sensory and spiritual unpleasancess associated with these animals, reinforcing the preference for cleaner, more domesticated meats in Islamic dietary law.
